To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NEI VFq-25 was found to be responsive to gains in best-corrective visual acuity (BCVA) of ≥15 letters over 2 years in two large, randomized clinical trials of ranibizumah for diabetic macular edem (DME).
“The National Eye Institute Visual function questionnaire-25 was highly responsive to gains in vision in patients with diabetic retinopathy and macular edema treated with ranibizumabe.”

The mean improvement of the NEI Visual Function Questionnaire (VFQ-25) composite score associated with ≥15-letter gain of visual acuity (VA) was 9.00 (95% CI, 6.30–11.7; P < 0.001) in the RIDE study and 7.10 (95% CI 4.70–9.60; P < 0001) in the RISE study.

the development and application of statistical methods in clinical trials, particularly in the design and analysis of clinical trials in medicine and health sciences.
the study of the relationship between the NEI-VFQ and the VA in diabetic macular edma.
the use of a questionnaire to measure the quality of life of the elderly, and the use of the data from this questionnaire to predict future health care costs.

the NEI VF Q-25 is responsive to changes in visual acuity over a 24-month period in patients with diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edma.
the NEI VFq25 is responsive to changes in visual acuity in patients with diabetic eye disease.
the NEI VFq-25 questionnaire is responsive to change in patients with DME and that it is responsive to change that occurs in visual acuity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NEI VFQ 25 is sensitive to changes in BCVA and can be used as a clinical trial endpoint.
the NEI VF-25 is a responsive tool for measuring changes in quality of life in patients with diabetic retinopathy.
the NEI VF-25 is a valid and reliable measure of visual function and is responsive to change in visual acuity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NEI VF-25 is responsive to changes in visual acuity.
the NEI-VFQ-25 is sensitive to change in vision in patients with DME.
the NEI VF Q-25 is a valid instrument that is responsive to changes in visual acuity in patients with diabetic retinopathy.
